answer: At a community garden above a flood haven, agents bid to monitor seedlings on a knoll. Each plot has a signed lease and one daily observation slot; rewards are paid for plots whose images match a later random inspection, not for the number of accounts reporting them. To multiply income, a sybil operator must control additional leased plots, supply distinct time-stamped evidence, and risk a deposit on false reports. A landlord could issue fake leases or inspectors could collude, so plot maps and inspection assignments are public and appealable.
